CONGRESSMAN FIELDS' STATEMENT ON THE UPCOMING CONGRESSIONAL ELECTION | Representative Cleo Fields Skip to main content Phone:  (202) 225-3901 Email Me Address:  2349 Rayburn House Office Building Washington, DC 20515   CONGRESSMAN FIELDS' STATEMENT ON THE UPCOMING CONGRESSIONAL ELECTION July 21, 2026 Press Release WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congressman Cleo Fields released the following statement regarding his decision about the upcoming congressional election: “After a great deal of prayer and reflection, I have decided not to seek re-election to Congress, in the 6th District or any other district in Louisiana. Instead, I will be running to fill the unexpired term for the State Senate in the 14th District. I feel my calling to serve the people is better put to use back home than here in D.C., and I intend to answer that call.” Congressman Fields will be holding a press conference this Friday at 10 am in Baton Rouge, LA, location to be announced, with more details on his decision. For any questions, comments, or inquiries, please reach out to sydney.broome@mail.house.gov , or (202) 843-2045. ### Media Press Releases In the News Previous Newsletters

CONGRESSMAN FIELDS’ STATEMENT ON FATAL ICE SHOOTING IN BIDDEFORD, MAINE | Representative Cleo Fields Skip to main content Phone:  (202) 225-3901 Email Me Address:  2349 Rayburn House Office Building Washington, DC 20515   CONGRESSMAN FIELDS’ STATEMENT ON FATAL ICE SHOOTING IN BIDDEFORD, MAINE July 13, 2026 Press Release WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congressman Cleo Fields released the following statement after a 26-year-old man was shot and killed by federal immigration agents in Biddeford, Maine, the second fatal shooting involving ICE officers in less than a week: "This morning, ICE agents shot and killed a 26-year-old man in Biddeford, Maine. He was authorized to work in this country. He had a Social Security number. He was somebody's son, somebody's neighbor. And now he's gone. Just last week, it was Lorenzo Salgado Araujo in Houston, shot and killed on his way to work. He wasn't even the man those agents were looking for. Two shootings in one week. Two lives taken, and neither man was the target of an immigration enforcement operation. I'll say it plainly: although neither victim was in this country illegally, an immigration violation is not a death sentence. It never has been, and it never should be. But when federal agents can shoot people in our streets with no body cameras, no accountability, and no answers, that's not law enforcement. That's lawlessness. The families of these men deserve answers. The American people deserve a full, independent investigation into both killings. And Congress needs to demand that this administration get control of an agency that clearly has none. I'm praying for these families, and for every community that now looks at their own government and feels afraid." ### Media Press Releases In the News Previous Newsletters

Congressman Cleo Fields Appointed to Exclusive House Committee on Finance | Representative Cleo Fields Skip to main content Phone:  (202) 225-3901 Email Me Address:  2349 Rayburn House Office Building Washington, DC 20515   Congressman Cleo Fields Appointed to Exclusive House Committee on Finance January 10, 2025 Press Release Washington, DC – Today, Congressman Cleo Fields (LA-06) was appointed to serve on the House Committee on Financial Services, one of the most critical committees in Congress, following communication from the House Democratic Steering and Policy Committee. The committee plays a critical role in overseeing the banking system, housing, insurance, and securities and exchanges, making decisions that directly impact economic growth and financial security across the nation. “I am deeply honored by this appointment. The Committee on Financial Services addresses some of the most pressing issues of our time and I look forward to working with my colleagues to advance policies that benefit families, small businesses, and communities across the nation,” Congressman Fields expressed. CONGRESSMAN FIELDS INTRODUCES NFIP PREMIUM TRANSPARENCY ACT ALONGSIDE COSPONSORS | Representative Cleo Fields Skip to main content Phone:  (202) 225-3901 Email Me Address:  2349 Rayburn House Office Building Washington, DC 20515   CONGRESSMAN FIELDS INTRODUCES NFIP PREMIUM TRANSPARENCY ACT ALONGSIDE COSPONSORS July 1, 2026 Press Release WASHINGTON, D.C. – This week, Congressman Cleo Fields, along with Representatives Troy Carter, Mike Ezell, and Rob Bresnahan, introduced H.R. 9511, the NFIP Premium Transparency Act , legislation that would require the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) to give the more than 400,000 Louisiana policy holders enrolled in the National Flood Insurance Program a full, clear picture of what is driving their premiums and what they can do to bring those costs down: "Louisiana families pay more flood insurance premiums than almost anyone in the United States, and for too long they've been handed a bill with no explanation. They deserve to know why their rates went up, when they'll go up again, and what they can do about it. This bill does exactly that,” said Representative Fields. Louisiana has the most NFIP policies per capita of any other state in the country. Despite that, members of communities throughout the state routinely receive renewal notices with little to no explanation of what factors are driving their costs or how long they can expect their premiums to reach their full risk-based potential. For working families in flood-prone areas, many of whom are already living on tight margins, that lack of information can mean the difference between staying in their home and being priced out of it. “Since FEMA's Risk Rating 2.0 program went into effect, Louisiana families have opened their flood insurance bills with more questions than answers: why their premium jumped and what discounts they're missing,” said Representative Carter. “Louisiana has more riding on this than almost any state in the country. This legislation gives homeowners the information they've always deserved: a clear breakdown of their rates, real savings from mitigation, and a roadmap to full-risk pricing. CONGRESSMAN FIELDS STANDS WITH CBC AND NAACP TO CALL ON COLLEGE ATHLETICS TO OPPOSE DISMANTLING OF BLACK VOTING POWER | Representative Cleo Fields Skip to main content Phone:  (202) 225-3901 Email Me Address:  2349 Rayburn House Office Building Washington, DC 20515   CONGRESSMAN FIELDS STANDS WITH CBC AND NAACP TO CALL ON COLLEGE ATHLETICS TO OPPOSE DISMANTLING OF BLACK VOTING POWER May 19, 2026 Press Release WASHINGTON, D.C.  — This afternoon, Congressman Fields released his statement after standing alongside the Congressional Black Caucus and the NAACP to demand college athletic institutions publicly oppose the coordinated efforts to dismantle Black voting power currently taking place:    “Today I stood with my colleagues in the Congressional Black Caucus and the NAACP to deliver a clear message: we cannot support the SCORE Act or any legislation benefiting major athletic institutions that remain silent while Black voting rights are being systematically eliminated.  In the wake of the Supreme Court’s Callais decision, states across the South — including my home state of Louisiana — have moved rapidly to redraw congressional maps designed to dilute Black voting strength and undermine decades of hard-fought civil rights progress. This is a defining moral moment for our country. For generations, Black athletes have helped build college athletics into one of the most powerful and profitable industries in America. Yet at the very moment the same communities many of these athletes call home face coordinated attacks on their democratic representation, too many leaders have chosen silence. Institutions that significantly profit from Black talent have a responsibility to stand with Black communities when their fundamental rights are under attack. We have transmitted formal letters to SEC Commissioner Greg Sankey, ACC Commissioner James J. Phillips, Ph.D., and NCAA President Charlie Baker demanding their immediate engagement. CONGRESSMAN FIELDS’ STATEMENT ON SUPREME COURT BIRTHRIGHT CITIZENSHIP RULING | Representative Cleo Fields Skip to main content Phone:  (202) 225-3901 Email Me Address:  2349 Rayburn House Office Building Washington, DC 20515   CONGRESSMAN FIELDS’ STATEMENT ON SUPREME COURT BIRTHRIGHT CITIZENSHIP RULING June 30, 2026 Press Release WASHINGTON, D.C. —  This morning, Congressman Cleo Fields released the following statement after the Supreme Court upheld birthright citizenship under the 14th Amendment in Trump v. Barbara : “The Constitution won today. For over 150 years, the 14th Amendment has guaranteed that every child born on American soil is an American citizen with no exceptions. The Supreme Court was right to reject this administration’s attempt to rewrite that guarantee by executive order. This was never just a legal question. It was about whether a child born in Baton Rouge or Lafayette or anywhere else in our country has to wonder if their citizenship is secure. Today they got their answer. I’m grateful the Court held the line, and I’ll keep working to make sure every Louisianan’s constitutional rights are protected, not just on paper, but in practice.” ### Media Press Releases In the News Previous Newsletters

CONGRESSMAN FIELDS RELEASES STATEMENT REGARDING IRAN FRAMEWORK AGREEMENT | Representative Cleo Fields Skip to main content Phone:  (202) 225-3901 Email Me Address:  2349 Rayburn House Office Building Washington, DC 20515   CONGRESSMAN FIELDS RELEASES STATEMENT REGARDING IRAN FRAMEWORK AGREEMENT June 18, 2026 Press Release BATON ROUGE, L.A. – Congressman Cleo Fields today issued the following statement expressing his strong disapproval of the preliminary framework agreement announced this week between the United States and Iran: “Let me be clear about what this agreement actually is. After dragging the country into a conflict that was never a war of necessity, the President is now searching for an offramp from a war of his own choosing, and he is asking the American people to foot the bill for it. This war has been extraordinarily costly. It has cost us both in American lives and in America’s standing in the world. Families across Louisiana and across this country have absorbed the consequences of a decision made without a clear objective and without a plan to end it. And after all of that sacrifice, this deal delivers no tangible benefit to the people who paid the price. I take particular issue with the $300 billion figure at the center of this arrangement. The administration wants Americans to believe this is a costless win, but you cannot wave away a number that large with talking points. Whether it is framed as a private fund, a reconstruction plan, or something else entirely, the language is deliberately vague, and it should alarm every taxpayer and every member of Congress.  The American people deserve more than a hastily assembled framework designed to let the President declare success and move on. They deserve to know what this is going to cost, what we are actually getting in return, and why they were asked to bear the burden of a war that never had to be fought. I will be pressing for full transparency and for honest answers about use of the $300 billion. Congress and the American people deserve transparency around how their tax dollars are being put to use.” ### Media Press Releases In the News Previous Newsletters

CONGRESSMAN FIELDS ANNOUNCES $1.8 MILLION IN FEDERAL FUNDING FOR NORTHWESTERN STATE UNIVERSITY EQUIPMENT EXPANSION | Representative Cleo Fields Skip to main content Phone:  (202) 225-3901 Email Me Address:  2349 Rayburn House Office Building Washington, DC 20515   CONGRESSMAN FIELDS ANNOUNCES $1.8 MILLION IN FEDERAL FUNDING FOR NORTHWESTERN STATE UNIVERSITY EQUIPMENT EXPANSION September 1, 2026 Press Release NATCHITOCHES, LA — Congressman Cleo Fields (LA-06) today announced that Northwestern State University has been awarded $1.8 million in federal funding through the U.S. Department of Commerce's National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to support the university's Innovation Park Equipment Expansion (IPEX) Project. The funding request was submitted in collaboration with U.S. Senators Bill Cassidy and John Kennedy. The award will allow the university to purchase cutting-edge equipment for Innovation Park, including an AI supercomputer, laser cutters, and advanced 3D printers. “Innovation Park is a cornerstone of STEM education in Northwestern Louisiana,” said Congressman Fields. “This funding will expand research and innovation opportunities, empowering students to deepen their  STEM expertise and drive groundbreaking discoveries. It will give students the critical skills they need to lead the next wave of scientific and technological innovation, and give Louisiana employers the workforce they need to grow. I was proud to work alongside Senator Cassidy and Senator Kennedy to bring these resources home to Natchitoches and to ensure Louisiana institutions get their fair share of federal investment in research and workforce development.” The equipment is expected to expand research and innovation opportunities at Innovation Park, provide students with hands-on experience in high-demand fields, strengthen the university's ability to attract and retain top undergraduate and graduate students and faculty, and support Louisiana's broader economic development priorities in advanced technology, industrial engineering, and biomedical research. The award was made under NIST's Congressionally-Identified Projects program (CFDA 11.617). ### Me

CONGRESSMAN CLEO FIELDS RELEASES STATEMENT ON PASSAGE OF THE 21ST CENTURY ROAD TO HOUSING ACT | Representative Cleo Fields Skip to main content Phone:  (202) 225-3901 Email Me Address:  2349 Rayburn House Office Building Washington, DC 20515   CONGRESSMAN CLEO FIELDS RELEASES STATEMENT ON PASSAGE OF THE 21ST CENTURY ROAD TO HOUSING ACT June 24, 2026 Press Release WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congressman Cleo Fields today issued the following statement regarding the passage of the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act and President Trump's refusal to sign the bipartisan legislation into law: “Last night, the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act passed with overwhelming bipartisan support and now heads to the President's desk. As a cosponsor of this legislation, I have consistently supported it because it directly addresses the housing pressures facing working families across the 6th District. It cuts the cost of manufactured homes, blocks corporate investors from buying up single-family homes, locks in disaster recovery housing funds for states like Louisiana, and helps low-income homeowners afford basic repairs. This is the most significant federal housing legislation in a generation, and I'm proud my vote helped move it forward. This bill has no partisan strings attached. It passed both chambers with veto-proof margins because it works for American families. President Trump's decision to cancel the signing ceremony and hold this bill hostage over the unrelated SAVE Act, a voting restrictions bill that doesn't have the Senate votes to pass, is wrong. Families in Louisiana cannot afford to wait. I am calling on President Trump to sign this bill into law now.” ### Media Press Releases In the News Previous Newsletters
